alt.en: A sepia photograph of a long, low, whitewashed cottage with a thick thatched roof and two chimneys, beside an empty dirt road. Its windows have dark wooden shutters, two signboards hang either side of the door, and a wooden wheelbarrow stands in the road.
alt.es: Fotografía en tono sepia de una casita larga y baja, encalada, con un grueso tejado de paja y dos chimeneas, junto a un camino de tierra vacío. Sus ventanas tienen postigos oscuros de madera, hay dos letreros a cada lado de la puerta y una carretilla de madera en el camino.

caption.en: The thatched cottage at Alloway in Ayrshire where Robert Burns, who gave Auld Lang Syne its words, was born in 1759, photographed by George Washington Wilson between 1870 and 1890.
caption.es: La casita con tejado de paja de Alloway, en Ayrshire, donde nació en 1759 Robert Burns, el autor de la letra de Auld Lang Syne, fotografiada por George Washington Wilson entre 1870 y 1890.

source: Geboortehuis van dichter Robert Burns (Birthplace of the poet Robert Burns), albumen print from an album, 116 x 191 mm; printed inscription "Burns' Cottage. Alloway. Ayr. 90. G.W.W."; album caption "Burns' Cottage at Alloway"
licenceEvidence: Rijksmuseum record https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/200777166 gives rights https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark). Photograph by George Washington Wilson (died 1893), made 1870 to 1890: PD by age (see rights.md).

alt.en: An engraved page of music headed "Auld lang syne.", numbered 413 and page 426, with the first verse and chorus under the notes on two staves, the other four verses below in two columns, and a footnote: "Some Sing Kiss in place of Cup."
alt.es: Página de música grabada con el encabezado "Auld lang syne.", con el número 413 y la página 426, con la primera estrofa y el estribillo bajo las notas en dos pentagramas, las otras cuatro estrofas debajo en dos columnas y una nota al pie: "Some Sing Kiss in place of Cup."

caption.en: Auld lang syne as No. 413 of The Scots Musical Museum, volume 5, the earliest known printing of Burns's words (1796), to the older, slower tune and signed Z, here in the volume's 1839 Edinburgh reissue.
caption.es: Auld lang syne como n.º 413 del quinto volumen de The Scots Musical Museum, la primera impresión conocida de la letra de Burns (1796), con la melodía antigua y más lenta y firmada con una Z, aquí en la reedición del volumen hecha en Edimburgo en 1839.

source: The Scotish Musical Museum, vol. 5 (Edinburgh: William Blackwood and Sons; London: Thomas Cadell, 1839), originally published by James Johnson; p. 426, No. 413, "Auld lang syne"
library: University of Western Ontario (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Engraved page first issued 1796, this printing Edinburgh 1839; James Johnson died 1811, Stephen Clarke 1797, Burns 1796. The Internet Archive record states no licence or restriction. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: An engraved page of music headed "Should auld acquaintance be forgot.", number 68, marked Allegretto in 2/4, with a voice part and piano, a second voice in the bass clef joining for the chorus, and the words of the first verse and chorus under the notes.
alt.es: Página de música grabada con el encabezado "Should auld acquaintance be forgot.", número 68, marcada Allegretto en 2/4, con una voz y piano, una segunda voz en clave de fa que se une en el estribillo y la letra de la primera estrofa y el estribillo bajo las notas.

caption.en: No. 68 of George Thomson's Select Collection of Original Scottish Airs, volume 2, which in 1799 first set Burns's words to the lively tune sung at New Year today, here in a copy issued in 1801.
caption.es: El n.º 68 del segundo volumen de la Select Collection of Original Scottish Airs de George Thomson, que en 1799 unió por primera vez la letra de Burns a la melodía alegre que se canta hoy en Año Nuevo, aquí en un ejemplar publicado en 1801.

source: George Thomson, A Select Collection of Original Scottish Airs for the Voice, vol. 2 (Edinburgh: G. Thomson; the 1799 volume, this copy issued 1801), No. 68, "Should auld acquaintance be forgot", Allegretto, with the note "The Sym. & Accompt. simplified as above by Mr. K. 1801"
